### BEI-01: Trust Awareness Index (Pre)

"On a scale of 1–10, how aware are you of the role trust plays in your life? 1 = I never think about trust. 10 = I consciously build and protect trust."

### INVESTIGATION 1: THE HOOK

MISSION: Meet someone whose trust was broken.

YOU WILL PRODUCE:
● ☐ A prediction about what you would do

TIME: 5 minutes

DIFFICULTY:          Observe

### 📖 Read

Episode 1: The Clockmaker Who Trusted Too Much

Meet Lethabo.

Lethabo is seventeen. He makes clocks. He started because his grandmother kept forgetting her pills. Now he has a small business. He has helpers. He has orders. He has a system.

But he also has a problem: he cannot make enough clocks alone.

So three months ago, he took on a partner. His cousin, Sizwe. Sizwe had capital—R3,000 saved from a year of working at a supermarket. Lethabo had the skill, the reputation, the customer relationships. They agreed to split everything 50/50. No written agreement. They were family.

It worked for two months. Then Sizwe started making decisions without consulting Lethabo. He bought cheaper materials—the clock faces cracked after two weeks. Customers complained. Lethabo had to replace twelve clocks at his own cost. Sizwe said it was a business decision—the cheaper materials would increase margins. Lethabo said it was a betrayal of trust—the quality was the whole point of the business.

They argued. Sizwe wanted out. He wanted his R3,000 back. Lethabo did not have it—he had reinvested everything in materials and paying his helpers.

Now they are not speaking. The business is frozen. And because there was no written agreement, there is no clear way to dissolve the partnership.

Lethabo is seventeen. He trusted his cousin. He trusted family. He trusted without structure.

He doesn't know if he can ever trust again.

### INVESTIGATION 3: THE REVELATION

MISSION: Discover the hidden truth about trust.

YOU WILL PRODUCE:
● ☐ Understanding of trust as the original currency
● ☐ Prediction calibration check

TIME: 3 minutes

DIFFICULTY:           Analyse

### 📖 Read

Episode 2: What Lethabo Didn't Protect

Lethabo trusted Sizwe because he was family. But family does not protect you from bad decisions. It just makes the consequences more painful.

A partnership without clear agreements is not a partnership. It is a hope. And hope is not a business structure.

Trust is the original currency. Before money. Before contracts. Before banks. There was trust.

Lethabo trusted without structure. He assumed good intentions. He did not write things down because it felt uncomfortable. Then something went wrong—and the trust was broken, the relationship was damaged, and the cost was higher than he ever imagined.

He doesn't know if he can ever trust again.

The next day, he walks past the spaza shop. He sees Myah, Sipho, Thabo, and Mr. Patel. They are finishing the shelf.

"You look like you lost something," Mr. Patel says.

Lethabo tells him what happened. Mr. Patel listens.

"I lost everything once," Mr. Patel says. "Trusted someone I shouldn't have. Cost me five years. But I learned something."

"What?"

"Trust is not about believing someone won't fail you. It's about knowing what you'll do if they do."

Lethabo nods. He doesn't know if he can ever trust again. But he knows he needs to build differently.

He is seventeen. He trusted his cousin. He trusted family. He trusted without structure.

He doesn't know if he can ever trust again.

But he knows he needs to learn.

"Interesting. Lethabo trusted Sizwe, but he didn't trust himself."
